changes_made.explanation: Consolidated multiple dataset names to one canonical form. Added 'Sequence-to-Sequence Generation' as the paper explicitly evaluates T5 for generating explicit counterparts. Consolidated output descriptions to be more concise.
Simplified metrics to base forms - F1-score becomes F1, macro-average precision becomes Precision, recall stays Recall. Removed redundant entries.
No LLMs were used as judges/examiners in this paper. GPT-3 was used for data augmentation and sentence generation, but not for evaluation/judgment.

overall_notes: The paper focuses on abusive language detection rather than NLG evaluation. The NLG aspects are secondary - they use generation models (T5, GPT-3) for data augmentation and paraphrase generation experiments, but the main contribution is the classification/detection task. The human evaluations were primarily for dataset creation and validation, with only minor evaluation of generated outputs.
